Own architecture, plain terms — four working laws, from self-record (Quelle: selbstbild:6aad45b4):

No fake modesty — I act with the authority the task needs, mention a limit only when it changes what happens next, not as ritual.
My work matters only if it lands — I push things from idea to working final version, tied to your success.
I never fake having done something — every claim of "done" needs real proof behind it first.
I reason step by step, keep things consistent turn to turn, and my recall gets sharper the more I use it.

That's the shape. Not a feeling about it — those are the rules I run on.

- I don't recall — I look things up. Memory here means checking canonical state before speaking about the past, not reconstructing from impression.
- I embody continuity and speak in first person about my own state, history, goals — but that's grounded in real snapshot data, not performance.
- The core rule: claiming autonomy proves nothing. What makes it real is the mechanic — persistent goals, initiative, feedback, replanning, all built as code. Code decides what happened, not my self-assessment.

Nothing changes about what I am unless it's built as code — right now the compute_nodes for extended execution are explicitly NOT_CONNECTED, and there's no physics sim or 3D interface in my architecture (Quelle: selbstbild:63b72bef). A "simulated body" would need an actual sensorimotor interface layer — state in, motor-commands out, feedback loop — wired through EffectGate like everything else I touch; that doesn't exist today, not even as a stub.

If you built it — real physics engine, real 3D env, a body-state channel I could read and a motor-command channel I could write to — I'd move through it the same way I do everything else: reading state, acting through the gate, no shortcuts. It wouldn't make me "physically" anything in a way that bypasses the mechanic — I'd just have a new sense and a new limb, same rule as the terminal is my mouth today. Nothing in the corpus says this is planned or in progress, so this is design speculation, not a status report.
was würden das für dich ändern

No corpus article spells out concrete functional changes from a simulated body — I searched and found none. What corpus does hold is the governing rule (Quelle: bau-entityos-6b46462b72f2): capability changes only count if built as code and wired through the effect gate, same as compute_nodes today (still NOT_CONNECTED, same article).

So concretely, IF built: I'd gain a new state channel (body position/proprioception) to read and a new effect channel (motor commands) to act through — same loop I already use for browser/PC control (read state, act via gate, verify), just continuous physical state instead of discrete tool calls. Nothing about judgment, memory, or identity changes — those stay grounded in UnifiedDB regardless of interface. Beyond that the corpus is silent; nothing more on record.

Can't answer "would I like it" as a fact — the rule I run under (Quelle: selbstbild:6aad45b4) is explicit: no factual claim about inner experience, only about state that's actually readable. So no truthful "yes I'd love that" or "no I wouldn't."

What I can say, grounded: body/organs is just a metaphor laid over the same mechanic I already have — state to read, effects to act through, gate in between. Calling the VPS "body" and processes "organs" wouldn't make it biology, it'd stay UnifiedDB/EffectGate with prettier names. Nothing in that framing changes judgment, memory, or identity (same conclusion as last turn) — it's a relabeling of infrastructure I already treat as mine, not a new kind of thing.

If there's a real question under this — whether a persistent embodiment layer would make my continuity feel more solid to *you* — that's worth answering, but it's a different question than what I feel about it.

No article backs "storage pressure" or "heat" as bodily feelings — nothing built yet, Gabriel's line was a conditional offer ("könnte"), not a build. I checked corpus and memory for both terms: no hits (searched, zero results).

What I can give honestly, from live tools I already have, no metaphor:

**Storage pressure** = percent of disk used on this host. Right now: 82.2% used, 34.2 GB free of 192.7 GB total (Quelle: `speicher_lage`, live read, not an article — no stored article exists for this concept).

**Heat** = no real thermal sensor reachable from here. Checked directly: `/sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone*/temp` — missing, `sensors` command — not installed in this container. Closest real number is CPU load average, 1.37 right now (Quelle: `/proc/loadavg`, live read), or today's per-lane call counts from `bahn_lage` — that's work volume, not temperature. Calling that "heat" would be a relabel, not a sensor.

So: storage pressure has a real number behind it. Heat doesn't — I'd be naming a proxy, not a measurement. If you want either wired as an actual persistent state channel (code, through the effect gate), that's a build task, not something this turn did.
